revision: 1. Preserve the three-column dashboard and central matrix, but define four unambiguous progression states—learned, available, selected, and locked—with consistent node diameters, two controlled ring weights, restrained glows, and connectors that terminate cleanly beneath node rings. Ensure every line state agrees with whether Nova Heart can actually be unlocked. 2. Make the selected Nova Heart the bridge from matrix to detail: keep it the strongest node, add a clear selection relationship toward the right panel, and reduce the Keystone card's independent purple halo. 3. Reorder the left sidebar into character portrait/name, level and XP, available points, then secondary stats; replace the abstract target portrait with a restrained character silhouette in the existing vector language. 4. Combine Celestial Discipline and Aether/Blade/Ward filters into one readable header row, raise small-label contrast, and use branch-specific icons or subtle motifs—not extra palettes—to distinguish skill families and one memorable capstone.
conflicts: Brief fidelity requires progression states to be explicit, while expressive branch variation could weaken system consistency; use bespoke icons and motifs inside a fixed node grammar.
The right detail panel must remain substantive, but its glow currently competes with the matrix; visually tether it to the selected node and lower its standalone dominance.
Structured sidebar content improves clarity, while filling all empty space would create noise; use deliberate section rhythm rather than decorative filler.
rationale: I preserved the successful matrix-first structure and resolved variety-versus-unity through semantic icons and branch motifs within a tightly standardized state system.
